The company categorizes this exposure into four main types: interest rate risk, which involves yield curve levels and credit spreads; equity price risk, relating to individual equities and indices; currency rate risk, involving spot and forward prices of currencies; and commodity price risk, covering assets such as crude oil, natural gas, and metals (Goldman_Sachs, Item 4).

To manage these exposures, Goldman Sachs employs a framework that includes monitoring compliance with established limits, diversifying exposures, controlling position sizes, and evaluating economic hedges (Goldman_Sachs, Item 4). The company acknowledges that its risk management models rely on assumptions about correlations among asset classes, which may prove ineffective during market stress when previously uncorrelated indicators become correlated or vice versa (Goldman_Sachs, Item 1A). Consequently, the firm notes that it has incurred and may continue to incur losses due to these limitations in historical data usage and model effectiveness (Goldman_Sachs, Item 1A).
